column3: Definition 1 sets tau=-infinity for non-antimagic G and quantifies 0<=s<=t. Conjecture 4 is a genuine downward-closure assertion, not the tautology suggested by the maximum notation. Deleting a P3 changes the available label interval and all vertex sums; no relabelling mechanism for arbitrary G survives.

Universal finite p* must cover every smooth Euler blow-up, not one self-similar profile. Compact support on the entire half-open spacetime may create a vacuous literal reading; that is a wording correction without credit. Source Conjecture 5 and Remark 4.2 distinguish smooth from C1,alpha solutions; no universal norm estimate is supplied.

Nonpositive linear spectrum after removing N neutral modes is insufficient for nonlinear orbital stability. Need control of higher-order centre dynamics for every nonsmallest binding radius and every N; no coercive normal-form estimate is available here.

Source Conjecture 2.2 quantifies typical configurations in algebraic or topological senses. A periodic grazing example is exceptional and does not refute typicality. Proposition 5.5 is conditional on bounded complexity, not a proof of it.

All k>=5 requires control of every step d through 2^k-2 as well as exact special-step values. Source explicitly derives Conjecture 5 conditionally from Conjecture 4 and Theorem 1.5. A finite sequence prefix cannot bound the unrestricted progression starting point; no certified automaton reduction established.

Primary Conjecture 2 and Theorem 8 match the nontrivial pseudoline-arrangement quantifier; Theorem 8 supplies c=1/845 for large n. No new credit; the record's strong-Dirac counterexample remark concerns a stronger claim. Main theorem statement read; complete proof/dependency replay not claimed.

Primary Theorem 1.2 proves the stronger linear-forest result for F with a colour-critical edge, covering F=K(k+1) and every path. Section 2 proof and Theorem 2.2 balancing argument read. Stability and Theorem 2.1 dependencies were not independently audited. Reproving the path case earns no credit.

Primary Conjecture 1.2 is accompanied by a computer-assisted argument; discussion reduces it to a specific hyperbolic-function inequality for x>=0,b>=T_infinity. Merely certifying sample parameters misses all coprime k>l>0. Existing numerical-proof boundary and any later analytic proof need audit before investment.

Both finiteness above delta/2 and infinitely many zeros above delta/2-epsilon for every epsilon are required. Source Conjecture 1.8 states both. Numerical zero searches prove neither eventual absence nor infinite recurrence; b4/delta transcription correction earns no credit.

Literal K2 plus an isolated vertex has m=1, spectral radius 1 and booksize 0, but is not itself complete bipartite. Primary explicitly ignores isolated vertices in edge-count extremal questions. Thus this exact finite witness exploits an omitted convention, not the intended order-sqrt(m) conjecture. Certificate retained; no discovery brief.

Literal target is identical in mathematical scope to assigned ID354392. Primary Conjecture 1.1 and Theorem 1.2 give an average-degree balanced-clique subdivision bound, stronger than existence of some f(k). Liu-Montgomery prior is cited but its proof was not fetched. No credit or new finite construction.

Same forall-k exists-f(k) minimum-degree assertion as ID354391. Primary states Liu-Montgomery confirmed it and gives a stronger quantitative theorem. Counting this rewording separately as a new outcome would duplicate the target; theorem bodies/dependencies not independently replayed.

Requires one A with uniform little-o error over x,chi,t as both q,T tend to infinity. Testing bounded character tables cannot certify uniformity or smooth-number tail cancellation. No full-range cancellation estimate or exact counterexample sequence identified.

Coefficients may have opposite slopes: x and -x have no common prime obstruction yet cannot both be positive primes. The source studies signed primes, so such a witness only exposes the positive/signed-prime domain convention. The admissible signed-prime tuple assertion remains deep; no credit for changing its domain.

The construction only proves the upper bound for all n; full equality needs a lower bound for every connected graph with fewer edges. Exhausting small n would give instances, not the universal matching/C4 colouring decomposition. No structural reduction to a finite certificate established.

K7 establishes necessity of seven colours, not sufficiency for all toroidal graphs. Existing nine-colour discharging does not provide a seven-colour reducible-configuration set; arbitrary toroidal graph counterexample search lacks a bounded obstruction theorem.

Balanced unit vectors with at least three image points must satisfy an exact second-eigenvalue and multiplicity claim for all n,d. Primary Proposition 4.2 supplies only multiplicity at least n-1; spectral ordering and exclusion of further n/2 eigenspaces are separate gaps. No exact violating Gram matrix certified.

Needs a Ky Fan bound for all injective configurations, not only regular simplices or cross-polytopes. Trace fixes the total sum but cannot by itself give the proposed sum of n largest eigenvalues. Tiny-n or ambient-dimension omissions are scope corrections without credit. No uniform subspace certificate supplied.

All fixed alphabet sizes and all distances below the linear threshold need 2^O(Aq(n,d)) enumeration. Trivial subset counting loses a logarithmic factor; a bound on the largest code alone supplies no balanced supersaturation. No full-parameter container mechanism found.

For each fixed cyclic bipartite H the constant may depend on H but not n. Counting arbitrary subsets of an extremal graph gives only a lower bound, while naive upper counting incurs log n. Particular even cycles or complete bipartite graphs cannot settle every H.

Fixed k requires polynomial rather than quasipolynomial time on all Ok-free graphs. A sparse-class algorithm does not cover dense instances, and no polynomial kernel or reduction to sparse instances is established. Definition of Ok must be preserved from primary before any hardness construction.

Requires the exact binomial sum for every admissible triplet. It includes the unresolved exact Erdos-Szekeres scale; checking small caps/cups or applying asymptotic bounds is insufficient. No general extremal recursion with matching upper bound obtained.

Weak polygons share endpoints in configurations with source-specific cap/cup axioms. Strong-polygon counterexamples at n=7,8 do not transfer. Need definition-faithful obstruction for one n or a universal recurrence; neither established.

All admissible (n,a,b) include the weak polygon family; index-shifting the binomial formula is not a solution. Geometric realizability need not hold for abstract configurations. No source-faithful finite counterexample or universal upper-bound induction established.

Antichain and pairwise union-size restrictions must hold simultaneously while minimum degree exceeds the proposed binomial coefficient. Uniform intersecting-family theorems alone do not address mixed levels. No compression argument preserving every degree or exact counterexample found.

Source proposes an upper bound n log^O(1)n, whereas literal equality would fail for trivial forests such as a single forbidden edge. That is an asymptotic wording issue without credit. Improving n*2^O(sqrt(log n)) to a polylogarithmic factor for all relevant ordered forests needs a new recursive bound.

All t and hypergraph ranks must satisfy the ceiling(3(t-1)/2) upper bound. Complete 3-uniform lower-bound constructions do not prove arbitrary minor-free upper bounds; ordinary graph Hadwiger cannot simply be imported through edge contraction. No finite obstruction mechanism identified.

Exact SU(2) decomposition could express squared projector overlaps via extremal-spin 6j symbols, a concrete route to rationality. Full target also needs the global maximum over all allowed coupling channels and sharp equality for all half-integer triples. No successor/proof-body clearance or monotonicity certificate; do not promote a rationality helper as full scope.

Primary Theorem 3 gives f(h,n)<=2^O(h*n*log n), and Corollary 5 explicitly confirms the Dujmovic-Morin conjecture using h<=n^2 and g(n)=O(n log^2 n). This routine published bridge already covers the target. Theorem/bridge read, full proof/dependency audit not claimed.

Primary Definition 4.2 defines Z(d) as the smallest matching number admitting an almost d-regular factor-critical triangle-free graph, not the maximum in the record. Maximisation would change the invariant. The intended odd-d minimum and its universal lower bound remain without a full-scope construction/obstruction here.

The four-colour theorem for cacti does not prove the literal target for every colorable connected graph. Primary concluding discussion distinguishes cacti from the general conjecture; retain global scope. No decomposition of arbitrary graphs into four locally irregular colour classes established.

Every ell>=3 needs a positive power separation for all sufficiently large m, comparing off-diagonal Ramsey functions. Known small ell cases cannot fix a uniform argument for each larger ell. No matching lower/upper exponent comparison survives for full scope.

For each S one must find NS working for every sufficiently large positive integer set. Typical-set estimates or any fixed additive improvement do not prove arbitrary S. No structural dichotomy or certificate reducing all exceptional sets to finitely many cases established.

Stronger target concerns max fA over all real x and all large sets A. Primary finite-range reduction still needs bounds on infinitely many sets of each allowed cardinality; it is not a finite computational certificate. Rational discontinuity enumeration for one A proves only an instance.

All j,k require simultaneous mass equipartitions in the asserted minimum dimension. Dimension counting gives necessity, not sufficiency; small-parameter obstruction computations do not extend automatically. No equivariant obstruction calculation settling arbitrary parameters supplied.

Equilateral 3-stick unknot supplies the upper bound 3sqrt(3). Arbitrarily many folds and crossings require a global width/linking lower bound, not a 3-stick optimisation. No universal inequality or smaller certified admissible ribbon identified.

Successor Janzer-Johnson-Leader arXiv:2210.13286 defines a (k,n)-shuffle as randomising the fixed ordered tuple 1,...,k and proves U2(n)=2n-3 for all n>=2 in Theorem 1.3. This is the intended target, not a new result. Rank-plus-support invariant proof read in part; full dependency replay not claimed.

Primary Conjecture 1 footnote reports a later proof; successor Theorem 1.3 settles a fixed pair, matching the primary intended 2-uniformity problem. The record's wording 'every subset of two positions' can suggest simultaneous uniformity of all pairs, a different invariant explicitly distinguished by the successor. Correct the scope before retirement of the literal wording; no credit for that correction.

The t-player success event is not defined by simply taking the measure of a tuple of independent intersecting families; primary game rules are essential. Dictatorship special cases do not settle the stronger limit for all intersecting strategies. No bound decaying uniformly in both strategy dimension and t established.

A single maximum independent set can have size alpha*n while the blocker must hit every maximum independent set. Picking one representative or using greedy covering does not ensure o(n); a counterexample needs a fixed positive density and a linear blocker along an infinite family. No such family certified.

D(k) graphs and their odd/even parity constraints must be taken from the source; ordinary graph orders alone are insufficient. Universal nonexistence below two linear thresholds requires a parity-aware lower-bound invariant. Source constructions above threshold do not establish it.

Record uses mixed tuple patterns (12,12) and (231,312) with OEIS A295928. Current source Theorem 3.5 counts avoidance of scalar patterns 231,312 with A026150 instead. Those are different avoidance conventions; no blanket 'source solved conjectures' retirement is justified. Recover the exact Bonichon-Morel target first.

Primary section 1.4 explicitly says the general coefficient-dependent Ife claim is false, since coefficients can make a preferred tree extremal, while the eccentricity specialization is true. The record mixes both. Recreating that parameter-choice argument or fixing its domain earns no credit; no independently replayed counterexample proof claimed.

All sufficiently large extremal point configurations must have one common angle anchor. Constructing self-similar examples proves only an upper bound on the minimum number of angles, not necessity for every minimiser. No rigidity/equality classification or infinite non-self-similar extremal family certified.

For each l>=2 and r>=2l needs a 2l-edge-connected r-graph with fewer than l disjoint perfect matchings. A single matching-packing obstruction at fixed degree is only an instance. Need a degree/connectivity preserving gadget family; none established beyond source's weaker upper bounds.

An unrestricted graph of genus g has arbitrarily many vertices by subdivision or attached trees, so the literal Vc maximum omits source restrictions. Fixing that omission is not discovery credit. Intended equality for every listed S needs the precise admissible embedded-graph class and designs outside the verified congruence family.

Numerical volume 5.33349 and a census minimum do not prove uniqueness over all spherical knotoids. Need a topological reduction to a finite list plus certified hyperbolic volumes, or an explicit smaller admissible complement. No such full-scope mechanism found.

Faithfulness of the constructed cyclic action would only establish the candidate index. Optimality over all klt Calabi-Yau varieties in every n>=2 is a separate global bound and cannot follow from checking through dimension 30. Current source has expanded conjectures; precise version alignment required before further solving.

Primary Conjecture 1 exactly matches the orientation claim and section 2 supplies an infinite counterexample family Tk with zig-zag high-Wiener orientations. This is a published source refutation, not a new finite target. Construction and initial proof setup read; complete maximality comparison and dependency audit not replayed.

Source Conjecture 10.1 has both Fitting-index and nonabelian-Fitting order assertions. Bounding G:F8(G) does not bound G:F(G). Direct product with a growing abelian factor also multiplies row zero counts, so it is not a fixed-m counterexample. No mechanism bypassing the source's remaining solvable-layer gap found.
